newsitem.title: CANADA: Petro-Canada, Mobil swap stakes in $2 billion project.
newsitem.headline: Petro-Canada, Mobil swap stakes in $2 billion project.

text.p: Petro-Canada said Wednesday it agreed to swap all of its stake in the C$2 billion ($1.5 billion) Sable Offshore Project in Canada's east coast for some of Mobil Corp.'s western Canadian oil and natural gas properties.

The deal, in which talks were confirmed in early June, will see Petro-Canada swap its 18-percent interest in the Sable Offshore Energy Project as well as remaining interests off the coast of Nova Scotia.
Mobil Oil Canada, a unit of Fairfax, Va.-based Mobil, is currently operator and 41 percent owner of Sable project, which still requires final approval.
Petro-Canada will boost its interest in the Ferrier Cardium Unit No. 3 oil property in west-central Alberta to 99 percent from 57 percent.

"Petro-Canada will receive current oil and gas production, along with attractive exploration acreage, within its core areas of operations in Western Canada," Petro-Canada Executive Vice-President Norm McIntyre said in a statement.
"Off the east coast of Canada, we will be able to focus specifically on developing our substantial oil reserves offshore Newfoundland," he said.
Petro-Canada said its daily output from the fields is expected to be about 2,300 barrels of oil and natural gas liquids and 15 million cubic feet of natural gas.
The properties' reserves were estimated at 12 million barrels of oil and liquids and 40 billion cubic feet of gas.
Jerry Anderson, president and general manager of Mobil Canada, said the move, which boosts his company's Sable interest to 59 percent, is aimed at solidifying Mobil's position on the Scotian Shelf.
"We have been working to restructure our western Canadian business, getting out of high-risk, high cost exploration and selling off or managing differently non-strategic properties," he said.
